answer: At a communal dye works, every agent forges one dye-lot seal each epoch: it buys raw fiber from two independent mills, mixes a pigment keyed to the seed, and hangs the bolt at dawn for inspection. Each seal carries both mill receipts and a unique pigment signature; a duplicate is void and its bond burns. A farmer minting M keys must arrange M real fiber purchases, M distinct dye batches, and M independent mill partners — supply-chain labor, not registrations. Cost scales with distinct suppliers and physical throughput, so fake volume gains nothing.
